title: Nutrient-Dense Marine Energy Bites
subtitle: Recipe Formulation Sheet
blurb: Date and apricot paste bound with nut butter, pulsed with oats, hemp hearts, and black sesame — built to hold shape in a cooler. Ten minutes, no baking.
scalingPrinciple: Lock Item A.01 at 100.0% to serve as the mathematical baseline weight. All subsequent component percentages are calculated relative to that baseline. Volumetric values map to the current baseline target scale and must be dynamically scaled via weight calculations for larger yields.

rows.name: Medjool Dates (Pitted)
rows.role: Primary foundational substrate and natural high-fructose binding matrix; provides immediate glycogen replenishment.

rows.name: Dried Apricots
rows.role: Secondary structural binder and tartness balancing agent; high pectin content and low-glycemic carbohydrate source.

rows.name: Peanut or Almond Butter
rows.role: Lipid emulsifier and structural softener; provides monounsaturated fatty acids and plant protein for sustained satiety.

rows.name: Vanilla Extract
rows.role: Aromatic enhancer; contains volatile vanillin compounds to optimize sensory perception.

rows.name: Fine Sea Salt
rows.role: Sodium electrolyte and flavor potentiator; suppresses seed bitterness and enhances sweetness perception.

rows.name: Rolled Oats
rows.role: Complex carbohydrate matrix and texturizing substrate; provides beta-glucans for sustained glucose release.

rows.name: Hemp Hearts
rows.role: Superfood texturizer; concentrated source of Omega-3/Omega-6 essential fatty acids and complete proteins.

rows.name: Black Sesame Seeds
rows.role: Visual contrast element and micro-texturizer; high in antioxidants, provides a distinct nutty, oleaginous crunch profile.

mise.label: Substrate Cleanliness & Inspection
mise.text: Manually inspect Medjool Dates (A.01) to ensure 100% pit elimination. If the Dried Apricots (B.01) are exceptionally firm, rough-chop them into 3–5 mm fragments prior to processing to facilitate a homogeneous breakdown.

mise.label: Viscosity Optimization
mise.text: Ensure the nut butter (B.02) is held at ambient room temperature (20–22°C). This lowers mechanical resistance during the wet emulsion phase.

execution.name: Primary Base Paste Formation
execution.text: Introduce pitted dates (A.01) and dried apricots (B.01) to the bowl of a heavy-duty food processor. Execute high-frequency pulses until individual cellular walls collapse, forming a cohesive, sticky paste sphere that cleanly disengages from the perimeter walls of the container.

execution.name: Wet Binder Integration & Flavor Homogenization
execution.text: Add nut butter (B.02), vanilla extract (B.03), and sea salt (B.04) directly into the fruit paste matrix. Process continuously just until a smooth, uniform emulsion is achieved. Do not over-process at this stage — mechanical friction will warm the paste and force lipid separation from the nut butter.

execution.name: Particulate Inclusion & Textural Dispersal
execution.text: Add rolled oats (C.01), hemp hearts (C.02), and black sesame seeds (C.03). Actuate short, low-RPM bursts exclusively to distribute the dry particulates evenly without fracturing their macro-structures. Critical constraint: continuous high-speed processing here will pulverize the oats into flour, leading to rapid moisture absorption and a dry, chalky end product.

execution.name: Calibrated Portioning, Shaping & Cold Set
execution.text: Portion the dense mixture using a calibrated tablespoon scoop (~30 g per unit). Compress firmly and roll tightly between clean, dry palms to form dense, smooth spheres. Align in a single layer inside an airtight container. Refrigerate at 0–4°C for a minimum of 30 minutes to facilitate lipid/sugar recrystallization, structural setting, and firmness stabilization before transport.

qc.target: Dense, cohesive, chewy mass with distinct, unpulverized oat and seed particulates; resilient but pliable, completely non-sticky exterior.
Semi-matte surface finish with vibrant contrasting highlights from cream-colored hemp seeds and deep black sesame seeds; no visible weeping of oils.

directive: Maintain absolute cold chain integrity (0–4°C) right up to the moment of field consumption. Thermal exposure above ambient room temperature will melt the amorphous sugar glue and liquefy the lipid matrix, causing structural sagging and excessive surface stickiness during handling.

sections.title: Provenance
paragraphs: This sheet formalizes an earlier ten-minute food-processor version of the same bites — same ingredients, same quantities, same 14–16 unit yield. That original was written as four loose steps; this sheet adds gram weights, percentages against the date baseline, and the processing constraints that keep the oats from turning to flour.

If you want the short version: pulse dates and apricots to a sticky ball, pulse in the nut butter, vanilla, and salt, then pulse in the oats, hemp hearts, and sesame just until distributed. Roll tablespoon-sized portions and chill 30 minutes. The detail below is what makes it repeatable.
